deploy.//: Migrations run before the app starts. Without this, a schema change deployed fine and then failed at runtime on the missing column — production sat three migrations behind for days, which broke login and left Accruals with no tables. `prisma` is a runtime dependency so the binary survives the production install, and it is invoked directly rather than through npx so boot never reaches for the registry. `migrate deploy` only applies committed migrations and is a no-op when there are none, so the trade-off is deliberate: a migration that cannot apply now blocks the release instead of shipping a build that cannot serve requests.
deploy.//healthcheck: Absent because it silently froze production. The probe fails deterministically — eleven straight `service unavailable` attempts across a 5m window, twice, against an app that boots cleanly and serves real traffic — and a failed probe makes Railway keep the PREVIOUS deployment live. Nothing announces that, so production sat several commits behind while builds went green: `POST /api/admin/report-schedules` returned 404 in production long after the route existed in main, because the container serving it predated the route. A probe that blocks every release is worse than no probe. Everything checkable on our side is ruled out: `/api` is HealthController's `@Public()` route so the guard does not reject it, the app listens on PORT (8080, matching the proxy's own `upstreamAddress` of [fd12:...]:8080), boot survives an unreachable database in ~2s, peak RSS is 150MB, and `lsof` shows one dual-stack `*:8080` socket answering over both 127.0.0.1 and [::1] — so `app.listen(port, '::')` is a no-op and NOT the fix. Before re-adding this, try deleting the manually-set PORT service variable so Railway injects its own; a hand-set PORT is the remaining candidate for the probe targeting a different port than the proxy. Re-add as `"healthcheckPath": "/api"` with `healthcheckTimeout` >= 300 (the window must cover `migrate deploy`, which runs in the start command above), and verify the deploy actually promotes before trusting it.
